newsitem.title: FRANCE: BoF's Gerard-3.0 pct deficit/GDP not untouchable.
newsitem.headline: BoF's Gerard-3.0 pct deficit/GDP not untouchable.

text.p: The Maastricht treaty criteria requiring countries to cut their deficits to three percent of gross domestic product does not have to be obeyed exactly, Bank of France monetary policy committee member Jean-Pierre Gerard said.

"Three point zero percent does not seem to me to be necessarily an untouchable limit, and like (European Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault) de Silguy says, there is room to manoeuvre," he said.
"The worry is to see it (the deficit) climb this summer to 3.8 percent, or even four percent," he added.

French newspaper reports have put France's public deficit at 3.6 to 3.8 percent of GDP. The government is waiting for the results of an audit of public finances which is due July 21, before announcing its own deficit forecast.
